personas.name: Nadia Okonjo-Bright
personas.who: 34, getting married in six weeks. Comfortable with software, not a power user. Already running four other wedding apps and, in the research's words, is 'not delighted by features; they want to be told what a normal day looks like, adjust three things, and stop.'
personas.context: Research state (A): 23:40, in bed, lights off, iPhone at 414 CSS px in portrait, one thumb, Warm tint already on from another SWS app. Fifteen minutes of attention left before she gives up for the night.
personas.task: Get the day-of schedule out of her head, hair through sparkler exit, about 28 moments, and produce something she can paste into the wedding-party group chat tonight.
personas.verdict: Got roughly two thirds of it typed in and then stopped, because she could not fix anything she had already entered and the QR code she wanted to print refused to draw. She would come back for the printed sheet, which she called 'the only part of this that looks like my wedding.'
delights: Time-order sorting really is automatic and really is invisible, she typed the ceremony first and hair second and they landed in the right order with no drag, no arrows, no thinking.

Enter adds the moment and focus jumps straight back to the Time field (verified: activeElement === evTime after Enter, both fields cleared). She got into a rhythm of type-tab-type-Enter and added nine moments without touching the screen twice.
Untimed moments are a first-class thing. 'Someone please make sure Grandpa Ted gets a plate' has no time and the app renders it with an em-dash and sinks it to the bottom instead of rejecting it.
No email field anywhere, no account, no interstitial. The research names this as the single loudest differentiator against pix.wedding, Lovecation and Perfect Wedding Timeline, and it is honoured.

frictions.what: She typed '7' in the Time field for the 7pm reception and the app silently recorded 7:00 AM. Same for '4' (ceremony) → 4:00 AM. Measured across 27 spellings: bare '7' → 7:00 AM, '07' → 7:00 AM, '4' → 4:00 AM, '19' → 7:00 PM. helpers.js:16 accepts any bare number 0 to 23 as a 24-hour value with no warning and no confirmation.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the failure mode the whole product exists to prevent. She noticed the 4:00 AM ceremony only because it sorted to the top; the 7:00 AM reception sat quietly in the middle of the list and would have printed that way. The app has a parse-failure warning for input it rejects and says nothing at all for input it silently reinterprets by twelve hours.

frictions.what: There is no way to change a moment. The only control on a row is a ✕ (verified: 1 button per row, accessible name 'Remove <what>', 0 inputs, no row click handler). Correcting a typo or moving the toasts by ten minutes means deleting the row and retyping the time, the description and the who/where from scratch.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research lists duration-based events as table stakes precisely because 'if the user has to hand-edit 30 rows after one change, they will go back to the spreadsheet.' This app is worse than hand-editing 30 rows, it cannot edit one. Her hair-and-makeup estimate changed once and she had to destroy and rebuild four consecutive entries.

frictions.what: 'Show QR' toasted 'Could not draw the QR' and nothing opened. Measured: with realistically-worded moments the encoder throws 'code length overflow' from 19 moments up (2,371-character URL against a 2,331-byte version-40 ceiling), and from 12 moments the code still draws but at 145 to 177 modules on a 300px canvas, i.e. 1 device pixel per module.
frictions.whyItMatters: A 28-moment wedding day is the normal case, not the extreme. One of the app's three share affordances is dead for every real timeline, and the failure message names no cause and offers no alternative, it does not say 'your day is too full for a QR, use Copy link.' The research lists the printed-QR-of-the-share-link as a headline differentiator.

frictions.what: Opened cold there is no starting point: an empty list and one grey sentence ('Hair, photos, ceremony, toasts, last dance, every moment lands in time order automatically'). No template, no worked example, no work-backwards-from-the-ceremony entry.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research is blunt: 'Every free generator in this space leads with this, Chronolio, Lovecation, 101 Planners, Kings Films. An empty grid asking the user to type times is instantly amateur.' In decision fatigue at 23:40 she wanted to correct a plausible day, not author one. The base ships an .empty component and this app does not use it (verified: no .empty node in the DOM).

frictions.what: Nothing ever says the work is safe. Every keystroke writes to localStorage but there is no saved flag, no timestamp, no confirmation (verified: no [data-saved-flag] element, no .trust stamp).
frictions.whyItMatters: The research's third complaint is data loss, 'I logged in yesterday and everything has been deleted!', and prescribes 'a small saved 12:04 timestamp' because 'silent persistence is worthless if the user has already been burned once.' She closed the tab and reopened it to check.

personas.name: Marguerite Vasseur-Hale
personas.who: 67, mother of the bride. Macular changes plus varifocals; reads at arm's length and turns text up everywhere she can. Confident with her phone, deeply suspicious of anything that looks like a form. This is the comfort-panel persona.
personas.context: Her kitchen, 09:20, bright window behind her, iPhone at 414px held in one hand while the other holds coffee. No time pressure, very little patience.
personas.task: Add the four family moments Nadia forgot (the grandmothers' corsages, the photo with Aunt Sylvie, the toast, the cake) and print two copies.
personas.verdict: Got the printing done and loved the result. Got precisely one moment added, because after she turned the text up the field for the couple's names became a sliver she could neither read nor type into, and she assumed she had broken something.
delights: She found the settings icon in the header without being told, and the panel is genuinely good: it opened as a 736px modal with focus moved inside, axe returned zero violations with it open, the live sample let her see the effect without closing it, and the permanent tick slot meant she could tell which option was on without judging colour. Largest took the root font from 16px to 24px and the setting persisted across a reload (sws.prefs = {"text":"xxl","contrast":"more"}).

The printed sheet at arm's length is, in her words, 'the nicest thing any of these have made.' 24pt italic serif names, letterspaced small-caps date, a hairline rule, tabular times. The base correctly resets --ui-scale to 1 for print so her 150% screen setting did not turn two pages into six.

frictions.what: With Largest text on a 414px phone, the 'The headline' field measures 27px wide and displays zero characters of 'Jessie & Sam'; its label overflows its 27px box and visually collides with 'The date' beside it. It is worse than it sounds because it also happens at the DEFAULT text size on a 320px phone, where the field is 28px and shows one character. Cause: the inline style="flex:1.6" at index.html:1292 computes to flex: 1.6 1 0%, so the headline gets a zero basis while its sibling keeps the base's flex: 1 1 12rem (192px, 288px at Largest) and takes the whole row.
frictions.whyItMatters: That field is the name on the printed document, the single most personal thing in the app. She could not see what was in it, could not tell whether her tap had landed, and concluded the app was broken. No overflow probe catches this: page overflow is 0px at every size tested, and axe is clean. It is only visible to an eye or a width measurement.

frictions.what: The time column is a hardcoded flex: 0 0 76px (index.html:1253) that does not scale with --ui-scale. At Largest every timestamp wraps to two lines, '7:00' above 'AM', inside a 76px box at 24px type, and rows grow to 175 to 247px tall.
frictions.whyItMatters: The time is the one thing she is turning the text up to read, and it is the one element that will not widen to hold it. Every other part of the row scaled correctly; this one broke into a stack. On a 320px phone at Largest a five-moment day is 354px per row, one row per screen.

frictions.what: The ✕ remove button is 36px tall at every comfort setting (measured 37×36 default, 43×36 at Largest, 51×36 at High contrast, the width grows, the height never does). It is the only control on a row and it is destructive.
frictions.whyItMatters: The system's own floor is --tap: max(44px, 44px * --ui-scale), and the research's non-negotiables list '44px+ tap targets' because of exactly this reader. Turning the text up made the target wider but no taller, which is the least useful axis for a thumb, and a mis-tap deletes a moment with no undo.

frictions.what: The parse-failure warning is 13.6px red text (index.html:1255 overrides the base's .warn callout component with a bare colour and font-size). At Largest it reaches 20.4px but stays a lone line of red under the button.
frictions.whyItMatters: The base ships a proper .warn block with a background, a border and a 3px left rule, the app throws it away for the smallest text on the card. High contrast does not help, because the rule sets an explicit colour rather than using a token.

personas.name: Kehinde “Kenny” Adeyemi
personas.who: 29, maid of honour, holding the bride's phone because the dress has no pockets. Not a planner, has never used a wedding app, and has been handed the job of 'keeping the day on the rails' an hour ago.
personas.context: Research state (B): 07:05, dim hotel room with the curtains shut, one hand (the other is holding a garment bag), phone at 414px, three people talking at her. The stylist has just texted that she is 25 minutes behind.
personas.task: Push everything from hair onward back by 25 minutes and get the corrected sheet in front of the photographer before she arrives at 10:30.
personas.verdict: Could not do it. She retyped eleven moments by hand, deleted the wrong one halfway through with no way back, and ended up photographing the screen and sending that to the group chat instead.
delights: It works with the hotel wifi captive portal unanswered, service worker registered, everything local, nothing waited on a network. The research names no-signal venues as a paid competitor's headline feature (EventSync) and this app just has it.
'Copy link' produced a working URL with the whole day inside it and no account and no expiry. When it worked, it was the fastest share in any tool she has used.

frictions.what: There is no shift, no duration, no reorder and no edit. The complete set of controls in the app is: Add to the day, ✕, Print for the wedding party, Copy link, Show QR (verified by enumerating every button). Moving the day by 25 minutes means deleting and retyping every affected row.
frictions.whyItMatters: This is the moment the app was built for and it has no verb for it. The research's second table stake is 'Duration-based events, not fixed timestamps. Change hair-and-makeup from 2h to 2h30 and everything downstream shifts automatically,' and its named differentiator is anchor-and-solve. Eleven manual retypes, one-handed, in a dark room, with people talking, is how a tool loses to a photograph of a spreadsheet.

frictions.what: Deleting is one tap on a 36px ✕ with no confirm, no toast, no undo, the row is gone and the state is written immediately (app.js:59-63). window.SWS.undo is loaded and available on the page (verified: typeof window.SWS.undo === 'function') and app.js never calls it.
frictions.whyItMatters: She deleted 'Photographer arrives, detail shots' instead of the row below it and had no idea what the who/where line had said. The portfolio shipped the shared undo runtime specifically for this and this app loads it and ignores it. On the one day when the data cannot be reconstructed from memory, the destructive action is the cheapest one to trigger.

frictions.what: Two identical moments are accepted with no warning and render indistinguishably (verified: 'Ceremony begins' at 2:30 PM added twice produces two identical rows, no duplicate notice anywhere in the DOM).
frictions.whyItMatters: Retyping eleven rows under pressure is exactly how a duplicate happens, and a duplicate on the printed sheet reads as a second event rather than a mistake.

frictions.what: Nothing in the app marks who a moment belongs to in a machine-readable way, 'Who / where' is one free-text line, so there is no way to hand the photographer only her rows.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research's strongest named differentiator is per-person cards ('Maya, your wedding day, 4 rows') and its eighth complaint is 'the generic hour-by-hour list doesn't answer the only question each individual has, which is where do I need to be?' She ended up reading rows aloud to three different people.

personas.name: Rui Marchetti
personas.who: 46, wedding DJ. Works 40 weddings a year, arrives with a printed sheet taped inside the booth, and will never open the app. Reads paper at arm's length in a dark barn with a phone torch.
personas.context: The barn, 18:50, the sheet is page 3 of 4 taped at eye level, one hand on a fader. He has never met the couple's coordinator.
personas.task: Know when the first dance is, when the toasts run, and whether the copy on his wall is the current one.
personas.verdict: The sheet itself is the best free wedding timeline he has been handed. He still had to text the coordinator twice, once because page 3 does not say whose wedding it is, once because nothing on it says when it was printed.
delights: The typography. 24pt italic serif names, letterspaced small-caps date, a 60pt hairline rule, 12pt tabular times right-aligned in their own column, and the who/where line in 9.5pt italic underneath. Verified in the generated PDF at Letter: this is the editorial/stationery register the research says the market actually wants, not a screenshot of a UI.

The print stylesheet is real. Header, footer, tip pill, comfort button, the warm-tint overlay and the whole screen UI are all hidden; the sheet is the only thing on the paper; a beforeprint listener re-renders it so Ctrl+P never prints a stale one. Ten moments = 1 page, 100 moments = 8 pages, no clipping, no navigation chrome.
Real URLs survive on paper. A 94-character Google Maps link in a moment wraps cleanly at the slashes rather than running off the sheet (verified in the generated PDF).

frictions.what: Only page 1 carries the header. A 100-moment day prints as 8 Letter pages and pages 2 to 8 have no couple's names, no date, no page number (verified: page 2 of the generated PDF begins '7:36 AM Moment 13' with nothing above it).
frictions.whyItMatters: This document's whole point is that it gets separated and handed around, 'one for the planner, the DJ, the photographer,' as the app's own copy says. The page taped to his wall is anonymous. A running header is a two-line CSS change (position:running / @page margin box, or simply repeating the head as a thead).

frictions.what: No version stamp and no print date anywhere on the sheet. The only date on it is the wedding date the couple typed.
frictions.whyItMatters: The research's sixth complaint is precisely this, 'after a last-minute change, everyone is holding a different version and nobody knows which is current, the classic cause of a groomsman showing up an hour late', and prescribes 'Version 4, revised Fri 3:40 PM' on every printout, noting 'this costs almost nothing to build and no free competitor does it.' He cannot tell his page 3 from the one printed two days earlier.

frictions.what: Untimed moments print with a completely blank time cell (#sheet .ev .t is set to '' when minutes is null, app.js:76). On screen they show an em-dash; on paper they show nothing.
frictions.whyItMatters: A blank time next to 'Someone please make sure Grandpa Ted gets a plate' reads as a printing error or a time that got lost, not as a deliberate 'whenever'. The screen already has the right answer.

frictions.what: Every printed copy ends with 'Breathe. Everything else is somebody else's job today.' (app.js:81) in 9pt grey italic.
frictions.whyItMatters: It is a lovely line for the couple and an odd one on the operational document a paid vendor tapes to a wall. It is also the last thing on the page where the print date should be.

personas.name: Ines Calvo
personas.who: 38, blind, NVDA on Windows and VoiceOver on iOS, keyboard only. Her sister is getting married and Ines is the organised one in the family. Has abandoned two wedding apps this month.
personas.context: Desk, 1280px window, headset, NVDA at a fast rate, no time pressure and very high standards.
personas.task: Add six moments, remove one she got wrong, and read the day back to confirm it.
personas.verdict: Added the six, which more than half the category cannot manage. But she never learned that one of them had been rejected, and she never heard a single confirmation that anything had been added or removed.
delights: The tab order is short, orderly and completely named: settings → tip jar → headline → date → time → what → who → Add to the day → Print → Copy link → Show QR → footer link. 12 stops, zero unnamed controls, zero traps (verified by walking Tab 12 times and reading activeElement).
Enter submits from any of the three fields and focus returns to the Time field, so the add loop is genuinely keyboard-native, better than most sighted-first tools.
The remove buttons are properly labelled 'Remove Hair & makeup begins' rather than 'button' or '✕'.
The QR dialog is a real <dialog>: Escape closes it and focus returns to the Show QR button that opened it (verified).

frictions.what: The time-parse failure is completely silent to assistive technology. #timeWarn (index.html:1310) simply drops its .hidden class, it has no role, no aria-live, no aria-describedby from the Time field, and no aria-invalid is set. There is no toast on this path either, and focus stays on the Add button.
frictions.whyItMatters: She typed 'sevenish', pressed Add, and NVDA said nothing at all. From her side the button did nothing. She pressed it four more times. Nothing in the app tells a non-sighted user that their moment was rejected or why, the one sentence explaining it is painted on screen and nowhere else.

frictions.what: #evList is a plain <ul> with no live region and no status message anywhere in the add or remove path. Adding a moment and deleting a moment are both completely silent.
frictions.whyItMatters: The app's central promise is that moments 'land in time order automatically', where a new row lands is the whole value, and she has to navigate the entire list to find out. A single visually-hidden status line ('Added at 2:30 PM, 4th of 6') would carry it.

frictions.what: No skip link, despite the base shipping a fully styled .skip component and this app having a <main id="main"> target ready at index.html:1287 (verified: zero a.skip nodes in the DOM). No <noscript> either.
frictions.whyItMatters: Two header stops before the content on every load is not fatal, but the target and the styling both already exist, this is a one-line omission. With JS blocked the page renders three cards of empty form fields and an empty list with no explanation.

frictions.what: The QR canvas has no role and no accessible name (verified: role null, aria-label null), so the dialog announces its heading and then nothing.
frictions.whyItMatters: She cannot know whether a code was drawn. The dialog could simply also render the link as selectable text, which would serve her and everyone whose camera fails.

personas.name: Marcus Trent
personas.who: 52, groomsman and the bride's uncle. Receives the timeline as a link in a WhatsApp group of fourteen people. Taps things quickly and reads confirmations slowly. Has no interest in installing anything.
personas.context: On a bus, 17:30, low battery, Android Chrome at 414px, one thumb, glare on the screen.
personas.task: Find out what time he needs to be at the hotel and keep the link somewhere he can find it again.
personas.verdict: Got his answer in four seconds, which is genuinely excellent, and then destroyed his own copy of the link with a reflex tap, and later walked around with a version that had been superseded without knowing.
delights: Tapping the link loaded the whole day instantly with no app store, no account, no cookie banner and no email capture. Two moments in from a 221-character URL. This is the app at its best and it is better than every incumbent in the research.
It loaded offline on the bus with no signal, the timeline travels inside the URL, so there is no server to be unreachable.

frictions.what: Because he had opened the app once before and typed a test line, arriving at the link fired a native confirm(): 'Open the shared timeline “Jessie & Sam”? Your current timeline (1 moments) will be replaced.' He tapped Cancel out of reflex, and the app then strips the hash regardless of the answer (app.js:136, verified: location.hash length 0 after declining). The link is gone from the address bar and he had to go back and find the message again.
frictions.whyItMatters: Declining should be free. Stripping the payload on the decline path punishes the cautious answer and turns a reversible tap into a lost document. It also reads as the app having eaten the link. (Credit where due: the underlying protection is right, his own data survived intact, which is more than most.)

frictions.what: Nothing marks the loaded timeline as somebody else's, or as a snapshot. The title field is editable, the Add button is live, the ✕ buttons are live, and there is no read-only mode, no 'shared by' line and no timestamp (verified: no readonly affordance, #addEv enabled).
frictions.whyItMatters: He now holds a fully editable local copy that looks exactly like the master. When the ceremony moved 30 minutes the couple sent a new link, but his phone still had the old one saved and looked authoritative. This is the research's version-drift complaint arriving through the app's own share feature: 'everyone is holding a different version of the timeline and nobody knows which is current.'

frictions.what: 'Copy link' is the only way to get the URL out, and when the clipboard write is refused the app toasts 'Could not copy' and offers nothing else, the link is never displayed anywhere he could select it (verified: 'Could not copy' on a browser without clipboard permission; no visible URL text in the DOM).
frictions.whyItMatters: Clipboard writes are refused in in-app browsers, over plain http, and in some Android WebViews, exactly the contexts a group-chat link opens in. A dead end with no fallback on the app's primary share path.

frictions.what: Nothing on the sheet or the screen tells him what time to be anywhere as *him*. He scrolled the whole day looking for 'groomsmen'.
frictions.whyItMatters: Same root cause Kenny hit from the other side: who/where is prose, so the document cannot be filtered to a person. The research calls the per-person card the category's biggest unclaimed win.

worksWell: The printed sheet. Verified in real Letter-size PDFs through Chromium's print pipeline: 24pt italic serif names, letterspaced small-caps date, a hairline rule, 12pt tabular right-aligned times, italic 9.5pt who/where lines, 1 page for 10 moments and 8 for 100 with no clipping and no UI chrome. A beforeprint listener re-renders it so Ctrl+P can never print a stale sheet. This is the editorial register the research says couples actually want, and it is the app's whole reason to exist.

The add loop. Enter submits from any of the three fields, both fields clear, and focus returns to Time, measured. 200 rapid adds through the real path complete in 83ms, cap cleanly at 100 with an honest toast ('That's a very full day, 100 moments max') and, crucially, leave the user's typed input in the fields instead of eating it. 30 fast clicks on Add produce exactly one row.
Time-order sorting with untimed moments sinking to the bottom in insertion order, stable across same-time entries (verified: three 2:30 PM moments hold their typed order).

The comfort panel. Opens from the header, focus moves inside, axe returns zero violations with it open, the live sample previews the change, Largest takes the root from 16px to 24px, and the choice persists across a reload via sws.prefs. Page overflow was 0px in all eight comfort/viewport combinations tested (320, 414, 1280, Largest, roomy, Largest+roomy+High contrast, Easier reading, dark+warmth 3) and axe was clean in every one.

Text safety. Every user string reaches the DOM through textContent. Script tags, , 500-character words, ZWJ emoji families, RTL Arabic and Hebrew, '=1+1' and '__proto__' all render as literal text, 0 injected nodes, no title hijack, no prototype pollution, 0px overflow, zero console errors across every run.

Server-free sharing that actually works. The whole day travels in the URL hash, opens offline with no account, and the guard against a link silently destroying the user's own timeline is correctly implemented (confirm on the accept path, own data intact on the decline path).
Offline. Service worker registers, all assets are local including the QR vendor, and nothing in the core loop touches the network, the paid competitor EventSync sells this as its headline feature.
hurts: The headline field, where the couple's names go, collapses to 27px at Largest text on a 414px phone (zero visible characters) and to 28px at DEFAULT text on a 320px phone. Cause: one inline style="flex:1.6" at index.html:1292 that computes to a zero flex-basis against a sibling with a 192px basis. Page overflow stays 0px and axe stays clean, so no automated check sees it.

A bare number in the Time field is silently reinterpreted: '7' becomes 7:00 AM, '4' becomes 4:00 AM. The app warns loudly about input it rejects and says nothing about input it misreads by twelve hours.

Nothing can be edited, shifted, reordered or given a duration. The entire verb set is Add, Remove, Print, Copy link, Show QR. The one thing that always happens on a wedding day, everything slides, requires deleting and retyping every affected row.
Delete is one tap on a 36px target with no confirm, no toast and no undo, while window.SWS.undo is loaded on the page and never called.

The QR code is dead for a real timeline: the encoder throws from 19 moments up, and from 12 moments it draws at 1 device pixel per module inside a 300px canvas. The failure message names no cause and suggests no alternative.
The QR dialog's heading is invisible in dark mode, inline color:#111 (index.html:1337) on the UA's dark dialog Canvas measures 1.01:1.
The printed sheet, the product, has no running header on pages 2+ and no version or print-date stamp anywhere, which the research names as the cheapest high-value differentiator in the category.

Everything the app can be told to do is invisible to a screen reader after the fact: the parse-failure warning has no role, no aria-live and no aria-describedby; adding and removing moments are announced nowhere; there is no skip link and no <noscript>.

load() (app.js:38-43) checks only Array.isArray(d.events) and validates nothing inside it, while decodeTimeline() (helpers.js:58-62) validates every field properly. A structurally valid but wrong-shaped record renders '12:NaN AM' on screen and on paper, '-10:00 AM' for a negative value and '[object Object]' for a non-string, and a single null element throws an uncaught TypeError and silently renders an empty list.
The time column is a hardcoded flex: 0 0 76px that never scales, so at Largest text every timestamp wraps to two lines and rows reach 247px.

Cold open offers an empty list and one grey sentence, no template, no worked day, no work-backwards-from-the-ceremony start, which the research calls 'instantly amateur'. The base's .empty and .trust components are both shipped and unused.
Who/where is one free-text line, so the document can never be filtered to a person or a vendor, the research's biggest named differentiator is unavailable by data shape.
mostWantedNext: Editable rows and a day-wide shift: tap a moment to change its time, description or who, plus 'everything from here, later by 15 minutes'. This is the day-of verb the app is missing entirely.
Undo on remove, using the SWS.undo runtime that index.html already loads.

Confirm an ambiguous bare time instead of guessing: '7, did you mean 7:00 AM or 7:00 PM?', and widen the parser to accept 'noon', 'midnight', '2.30pm', '1430' and '2 30 pm', all of which are currently rejected outright.
A running header and a 'printed Fri 3:40 PM · v4' stamp on every printed page, plus a print-date line replacing the blank time cell for untimed moments.
Delete the inline style="flex:1.6", and let the time column and the ✕ button scale with --ui-scale and --tap.
A starting template, work backwards from the ceremony time with first-look and travel toggles, and the .empty component to introduce it.

Make the QR honest: draw it only when the payload fits at a scannable module size, and otherwise say 'this day is too full for a QR, use Copy link', with the link also shown as selectable text for when the clipboard is refused.
Per-person structure: a people field that is a list rather than prose, and a 'print everyone's card' batch, the research's strongest unclaimed differentiator.
Normalise the state shape on load the way decodeTimeline already does, so a damaged record degrades to a recoverable list instead of NaN on paper or a blank screen.
Announce the add, the remove and the parse failure to assistive technology, and add the skip link the base already styles.

scenarios.name: The standard battery (node design/stress.mjs wedding-timeline)
scenarios.method: Ran the shipped battery, then read design/stress.mjs to check what its app-agnostic probes actually touched in this app.
scenarios.result: 0 hard failures, every row reported clean. But the probes missed the app: stress.mjs:187 picks the first text input, which is #titleInput (the couple's names), and stress.mjs:188 picks the first .btn.primary, which is #addEv, so the 'bulk: 200 rapid adds' run typed 200 titles and clicked Add with an empty What field, adding nothing (nodes:0, textLen 492). 'rapid clicking' (461→492 chars) measured only the toast text. Consequently the axe scan, the keyboard-reachability scan, the touch-target scan and the print check all ran against an empty list, and the 'survives reload' row compared two empty states.
scenarios.defect: The battery's clean sheet for this app is close to vacuous. Its corrupt-storage probe also writes '{"broken":', invalid JSON, which this app catches correctly, and never tests the case that actually breaks it: valid JSON with a wrong shape.

scenarios.name: 200 rapid adds through the real add path, and the 100 cap
scenarios.method: Drove #evTime + #evWhat + #evWho + #addEv 200 times in a tight loop with realistic times and descriptions, then measured rows, stored state, the toast, the fields, page overflow, scroll cost, small targets and axe.
scenarios.result: 83ms for 200 attempts. Exactly 100 rows created and 100 events in localStorage (13,229 bytes). The 101st attempt toasted 'That's a very full day, 100 moments max' and left the user's typed input in the fields rather than discarding it. Page overflow 0px, two full-page scroll jumps in 11ms, axe clean with 100 rows, 113 focusable elements, zero console errors. Separately, 30 fast clicks on Add with a filled form produced exactly 1 row.

scenarios.name: Time parsing across 27 spellings a real person would type
scenarios.method: Called parseTime()/fmtTime() in-page over 27 inputs and recorded the rendered result for each, then confirmed the worst case end-to-end through the UI.
scenarios.result: Accepted: '2:30 pm', '2:30PM', ' 2:30 pm ', '14:30', '2pm', '9:05am', '12:00'→12:00 PM, '0:00'→12:00 AM. Rejected with the warning: '2.30pm', '2 30 pm', 'noon', 'midnight', '1430', '2-30pm', '2:30p.m.', '2:5', '2:60', '24:00', '13pm', full-width '２:30pm'. SILENTLY REINTERPRETED: '7'→7:00 AM, '07'→7:00 AM, '4'→4:00 AM, '19'→7:00 PM. Confirmed through the UI: typing '7' with 'Reception starts' renders '7:00 AM' with no warning shown and no toast.
scenarios.defect: helpers.js:16 treats any bare 0 to 23 as a 24-hour value. A couple typing '7' for a 7pm reception gets 7:00 AM with no signal of any kind, while eleven plausible spellings the app could accept are rejected outright and the warning text only offers two formats.

scenarios.name: Hostile text through the real add path
scenarios.method: Added 11 moments whose What and Who carried '', '', 500×'A', 400×'x ', a ZWJ emoji family, Arabic+Hebrew RTL, CJK+accented Latin, '=1+1', '__proto__', whitespace-only and 200×'e'; then queried for injected nodes, poison strings, prototype pollution and overflow.
scenarios.result: 10 rows created (whitespace-only correctly rejected with 'What's happening at that time?'). 0 injected script nodes, 0 injected img nodes, document.title untouched, no NaN/undefined/[object Object] on screen, ({}).polluted undefined. Longest rendered row 168 characters, the 500-char and 200-char inputs truncate at the maxlength/slice boundary. RTL, CJK and emoji all render without breaking the row. Page overflow 0px, offenders list empty, zero console errors.

scenarios.name: QR capacity as the day fills up
scenarios.method: Built the real share URL for 1 to 35 moments at both realistic and terse wording, ran the vendored qrcode(0,'M') encoder on each, and recorded the module count and the cell size the app would draw at (Math.floor(300/(count+8)), app.js:155). Then clicked Show QR on a 30-moment day and read what the user sees.
scenarios.result: Realistic wording: 1 moment → 221-char URL, 61 modules, 4px cells. 11 → 1,411 chars, 141 modules, 2px. 12 → 145 modules, 1px. 18 → 2,251 chars, 177 modules (version 40), 1px. 19 → 2,371 chars, THROWS 'code length overflow. (18988>18672)'. Terse wording (short What, empty Who) reaches 35 moments at 121 modules / 2px. At 30 moments the UI shows only a toast, 'Could not draw the QR'; the dialog never opens.
scenarios.defect: The QR path is unusable for a normal wedding day. It hard-fails from 19 moments and produces a code at 1 device pixel per module, physically unscannable, from 12. The error message names no cause and does not point at Copy link, which still works.

scenarios.name: QR dialog in dark mode
scenarios.method: Opened #qrDlg with the browser in dark scheme and computed the contrast of its heading and Close button against the dialog's resolved background.
scenarios.result: The dialog has no background declared (index.html:1336 sets only border, radius, padding and alignment), so it takes the UA's dark Canvas: rgb(18,18,18). The h3 carries an inline color:#111 (index.html:1337) → 1.01:1 at 18.7px. The Close button inherits app tokens and is fine at 15.53:1. In light mode the same heading is 17.4:1.
scenarios.defect: 'Scan to open the timeline' is invisible in dark mode, the dialog opens showing a QR code and a Close button with an apparently blank heading. Two hardcoded colour decisions in one line of inline style.

scenarios.name: The printed sheet, as real Letter PDFs
scenarios.method: Seeded a 10-moment realistic day, a 100-moment day and a long-content day; fired beforeprint the way Ctrl+P does; generated PDFs through Chromium's print pipeline at Letter; extracted the text with pdftotext and inspected page counts, headers and geometry; separately measured the print DOM at 414px and at 816px (612pt paper width).
scenarios.result: 10 moments → 1 page. 100 moments → 8 pages. Screen chrome is correctly gone: header.app, .screenonly, footer.colophon, #swsPrefsBtn and #toast all display:none; #sheet is the only content. Times are right-aligned and tabular, the who/where line is 9.5pt italic #666, the head is 24pt italic with a letterspaced date and a 60pt rule. Untimed moments print with an empty time cell (2 of 30 in the realistic day). Pages 2 to 8 of the 100-moment sheet carry no header at all, page 2 begins '7:36 AM Moment 13'. No print date and no version string anywhere. Empty-state guard works: Print with no moments toasts 'Add the day's moments first' instead of printing a blank page.
scenarios.defect: No running header on pages 2+, and no version/print-date stamp on any page, the research's sixth complaint, unaddressed. Untimed moments lose the em-dash they have on screen.

scenarios.name: Long and unbroken content on paper
scenarios.method: Printed a 94-character Google Maps URL, a 52-character hashtag and a 63-character unbroken Welsh place name in the What field, plus an 80-character headline, and measured .ev .w against the 816px paper box.
scenarios.result: No defect on the event rows: the maps URL wraps at its slashes and the 63-character word fits inside the 644px text column (scrollWidth === clientWidth for every row). #sheet .ev .w does compute overflow-wrap:normal, so a genuinely unbroken token over ~70 characters would overflow, but maxlength=120 and 12pt Georgia make that unreachable with real content. The 80-character headline is a different story: only 45 of its 80 characters render on the page, #sheet .head h1 (index.html:1264) has no wrap or shrink guard at 24pt.
scenarios.defect: A very long unbroken headline is silently truncated on paper. Realistic hyphenated double-barrelled names contain spaces and wrap correctly, so this is a boundary case rather than a daily one.

scenarios.name: Layout across eight comfort and viewport combinations
scenarios.method: Eight separate withApp runs over a 6-moment day: 414 default, 320, 414 Largest, 320 Largest, 414 roomy, 414 Largest+roomy+High contrast, 414 Easier reading, and dark+warmth 3. Measured page overflow, offenders, the time column, row height, the delete button and axe in each.
scenarios.result: Page overflow 0px and axe clean in all eight, no horizontal scroll anywhere and no violations at any comfort setting. But the time column is flex-basis 76px in every one of them: at Largest it holds 24px type, so '7:00 AM', '11:45 AM' and '12:30 PM' all wrap to two lines (74px tall) and rows grow to 175 to 247px (354px at 320px width). The ✕ button measures 37×36 default, 43×36 at Largest, 51×36 at High contrast, the width responds to the comfort settings and the height never leaves 36px, against a --tap floor of 44px.
scenarios.defect: Two elements ignore the comfort scale: the hardcoded .time flex basis (index.html:1253) and the .btn.small height used for the only per-row control.

scenarios.name: The comfort panel, driven from the header
scenarios.method: Clicked #swsPrefsBtn, inspected the dialog, ran axe with it open, clicked the Largest and High contrast option chips, closed with Done, re-measured the page and reloaded.
scenarios.result: Opens as a 376×736 modal inside a 900px viewport with focus moved inside, seven fieldsets (Appearance, Text size, Spacing, Reading, Warm tint, Contrast, Motion) and a Reset/Done footer. axe with the panel open: 0 violations. Clicking the chips set data-text="xxl" and data-contrast="more" and took the root font 16px→24px live. Done closed it, page overflow stayed 0px, axe stayed clean, sws.prefs persisted as {"text":"xxl","contrast":"more"} and survived a reload.
scenarios.defect: The panel itself is faultless. What it cannot reach is the app layer: the inline style="flex:1.6" on the headline field, the 76px time column and the 36px ✕ are all outside its influence, and turning the text up makes the first of those strictly worse.

scenarios.name: The headline/date field row at every width and text size
scenarios.method: Measured #titleInput, #dateInput and their labels, width, label line count, clipping and computed flex, at 414 default, 414 text:l/xl/xxl, 320 default, 320 Largest and 1280.
scenarios.result: #titleInput width by configuration: 1280 default 240px; 414 default 86px (≈8 visible characters); 414 Largest 27px (0 characters, label clipped and overflowing into 'The date'); 414 text:xl 51px (3 characters); 414 text:l 68px; 320 DEFAULT 28px (1 character, label clipped); 320 Largest 246px (fine, the row has wrapped by then). #dateInput holds 192 to 305px throughout. Computed flex on the headline label is '1.6 1 0%' against the base's '1 1 12rem' on its sibling. Page overflow is 0px and axe is clean in every one of these states.
scenarios.defect: The inline style="flex:1.6" at index.html:1292 sets a zero flex-basis, so the couple's-names field loses the whole row to the date field between roughly 300px and 700px of available width. Broken at the default setting on the most common small phone.

scenarios.name: Structurally valid but wrong-shaped localStorage
scenarios.method: Wrote 11 records into the wedding-timeline key, events as an object, [null], minutes as a string, minutes 1e999, missing what, what as an object, minutes 99999, minutes -600, title as a number, truncated JSON, and 10,000 events, reloading and inspecting the DOM, the console and the printed sheet after each.
scenarios.result: Booted in all 11. Invalid JSON and events-not-an-array are both shrugged off correctly. But: {"minutes":"abc"} renders '12:NaN AM' on screen AND on the printed sheet; {"minutes":1e999} renders '12:NaN PM'; {"minutes":-600} renders '-10:00 AM'; {"minutes":99999} renders '10:39 PM' with no complaint; {"what":{...}} renders '[object Object]'; a missing what renders an empty row. Worst: events:[null] throws an uncaught 'TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'minutes')' out of sortEvents (helpers.js:31) and the list renders completely empty while the record is still in storage. 10,000 events render in 927ms without error.
scenarios.defect: load() (app.js:41) validates only that events is an array. decodeTimeline() (helpers.js:58-62) validates minutes, what and who properly and caps at 100, the URL door is hardened and the storage door is not. A single bad element reads to the user as the app having deleted their whole day.

scenarios.name: The shared-link flow, accept and decline
scenarios.method: Encoded a two-moment timeline, seeded a different three-moment timeline as the user's own, and made full fresh navigations (via about:blank so init() genuinely re-runs) to the link with the confirm dismissed and then accepted; repeated with no local timeline.
scenarios.result: Decline: confirm reads 'Open the shared timeline “Ana & Priya”? Your current timeline (3 moments) will be replaced.' The user's own timeline survives untouched (3 rows, title unchanged), the guard works. Accept: the shared timeline loads, 2 rows, title field updates, toast 'Timeline loaded from the link'. No local timeline: it loads silently with no confirm, which is correct. In ALL cases history.replaceState (app.js:136/138) strips the hash, including after a decline. A loaded shared timeline is fully editable with no read-only affordance, no 'shared by' line and no timestamp.
scenarios.defect: Declining destroys the link, the payload is stripped from the URL on the path where the user said no, so there is no way to change their mind. And a loaded shared copy is indistinguishable from an original, which manufactures exactly the version-drift the research names as complaint 6.

scenarios.name: Keyboard-only path, delete semantics and the error channel
scenarios.method: Walked Tab 12 times logging activeElement; typed and submitted with Enter; submitted an unparseable time and inspected #timeWarn's ARIA and the focus; submitted '7'; deleted a row and inspected the toast, undo and SWS availability; enumerated per-row controls.
scenarios.result: Tab order: #swsPrefsBtn → #tipLink → #titleInput → #dateInput → #evTime → #evWhat → #evWho → #addEv → #printBtn → #shareBtn → #qrBtn → footer link. 12 stops, all named, no traps. Enter from #evWhat adds the moment, clears both fields and returns focus to #evTime. On an unparseable time: #timeWarn becomes visible with role null, aria-live null, no aria-describedby on #evTime, no aria-invalid, no toast, and focus stays on #addEv. On '7': no warning at all and the row renders 7:00 AM. Delete: 1 tap, no confirm, no toast, no undo button, while typeof window.SWS.undo === 'function'. Per row: exactly 1 button ('Remove <what>'), 0 inputs, no click handler. No a.skip and no <noscript> in the document.
scenarios.defect: The add loop is genuinely keyboard-excellent and the error channel is genuinely silent: a rejected moment produces no announcement, no toast and no focus move, so from a screen reader's side the Add button does nothing. Delete is irreversible despite the shared undo runtime being loaded on the page.

scenarios.name: Same-time ordering, duplicates and double submit
scenarios.method: Added three moments all at 2:30 pm (two of them textually identical) plus two untimed ones, then fired 30 clicks on Add with a filled form.
scenarios.result: Order held exactly as typed, 'Ceremony begins', 'Processional music starts', 'Ceremony begins', then the two untimed rows in insertion order. sortEvents is stable via its index tiebreak. Two identical moments were accepted with no warning and render indistinguishably. 30 rapid clicks produced exactly 1 row and then 'What's happening at that time?' for the remaining 29, because the fields clear on success.
scenarios.defect: Duplicate moments are accepted silently. Given that a time change currently requires deleting and retyping rows, double entry is a likely outcome and a duplicate on the printed sheet reads as a second event.

scenarios.name: Unicode on paper (environment caveat, not a defect)
scenarios.method: Printed a moment whose Who line contained '子安 花子 (Hanako Koyasu Photography)' and 'Émilie Ångström-Ñuñez' and extracted the PDF text.
scenarios.result: Accented Latin printed perfectly. The two 子 glyphs are absent from the PDF, but fc-list reports 0 Japanese-capable fonts installed in this container, so Chromium had nothing to fall back to from Georgia. This is an environment artifact, NOT an app defect; the same page on a real phone or laptop would fall back to a system CJK face. Reported here only so it is not mistaken for a finding later.

fixes.title: Delete the inline style="flex:1.6", it collapses the couple's-names field to 27px
fixes.rationale: Measured: #titleInput is 28px wide at DEFAULT text on a 320px phone (1 visible character) and 27px at Largest text on a 414px phone (0 visible characters, label clipped and overflowing into 'The date'). A unitless flex shorthand computes to flex: 1.6 1 0%, so the headline field carries a zero basis while its sibling keeps the base's .row > * flex: 1 1 12rem, 192px, and 288px at Largest. The date field takes the whole row. Marguerite could not see what she had typed and assumed she had broken the app; page overflow stays 0px and axe stays clean, so nothing automated catches it. Fix: remove the inline style and let .row > * handle both, or use flex: 1.6 1 12rem so the basis survives.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/index.html:1292 (and the same unitless pattern at :1304 for 'What', which is currently harmless only because its sibling at :1302 is flex:0 0 110px)

fixes.title: Stop silently turning '7' into 7:00 AM
fixes.rationale: parseTime accepts any bare 0 to 23 as a 24-hour value (helpers.js:16), so '7' → 7:00 AM, '4' → 4:00 AM. Verified end-to-end: typing '7' with 'Reception starts' renders 7:00 AM with no warning and no toast. Nadia's 7pm reception was recorded as a 7am one. The app warns loudly about input it rejects and says nothing about input it misreads by twelve hours, and it is the one thing this product exists to get right. Ask instead of guessing ('7, did you mean 7:00 AM or 7:00 PM?'), and while in there widen the parser: 'noon', 'midnight', '2.30pm', '1430', '2 30 pm', '2:30p.m.' and '2:5' are all rejected today and are all things people type.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/helpers.js:4-18 (parseTime, the bare-number branch at :16), surfaced at apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:93-94, warning text at index.html:1310

fixes.title: Make a moment editable, and add a day-wide shift
fixes.rationale: The complete verb set is Add, Remove, Print, Copy link, Show QR, verified by enumerating every button. Each row has exactly one control, a ✕. Kenny's stylist ran 25 minutes late and she had to delete and retype eleven moments one-handed in a dark hotel room; she gave up and sent a photo of the screen. The research's second table stake is duration-based events that shift downstream automatically, and its named differentiator is anchor-and-solve; the minimum honest version is tap-a-row-to-edit plus 'everything from here, later by 15 minutes'. Editing also removes the main cause of the duplicate rows the app accepts silently.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:48-65 (renderList, rows carry only the remove button), app.js:89-101 (add is the only mutation path)

fixes.title: Give the parse failure a voice, it is completely silent to assistive technology
fixes.rationale: #timeWarn simply drops its .hidden class: role null, aria-live null, no aria-describedby on #evTime, no aria-invalid, no toast on that path, and focus stays on #addEv (all verified). Ines typed 'sevenish', pressed Add, heard nothing, and pressed it four more times. The sentence explaining the failure is painted on screen and exists nowhere else. Give #timeWarn role="status" (or route it through the existing #toast, which is already a live region), point #evTime's aria-describedby at it, set aria-invalid while it shows, and move focus back to #evTime.

fixes.title: Make the QR honest, it hard-fails from 19 moments and is unscannable from 12
fixes.rationale: Measured against the real share URL and the vendored encoder: 18 moments → 2,251 chars, 177 modules, 1px cells; 19 moments → 'code length overflow. (18988>18672)' thrown; a 30-moment day shows only the toast 'Could not draw the QR' and the dialog never opens. Below the throw threshold, app.js:155 computes Math.floor(300/(count+8)), which is 1 device pixel per module from 12 moments up, the code renders but no camera will read it. A 28-moment day is the normal case. Either gate the button (draw only while the payload fits at ≥3px cells and otherwise say 'this day is too full for a QR, use Copy link'), or size the canvas from the module count instead of pinning it at 300px.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:150-165 (showQr, cell maths at :155, the bare catch at :162) and app.js:170-174 (the qrBtn handler)

fixes.title: Undo the remove instead of doing it instantly, SWS.undo is already loaded
fixes.rationale: One tap on a 36px ✕ deletes the row and writes state immediately, with no confirm, no toast and no undo (app.js:59-63). window.SWS.undo is present on the page (verified: typeof === 'function') and app.js never calls it; index.html:1276 loads sws-ui.js for exactly this. Kenny deleted the wrong row under pressure and could not recover the who/where line. The portfolio's stated position is that undo taxes nothing and a confirm taxes every correct tap. Snapshot the removed event, splice, then SWS.undo('Removed “First look”', restore).
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:59-63 (the remove button's onclick), runtime at apps/wedding-timeline/sws-ui.js:130-134

fixes.title: Put a running header and a print stamp on the printed sheet
fixes.rationale: Verified in real Letter PDFs: 100 moments print as 8 pages and only page 1 carries the couple's names and date, page 2 begins '7:36 AM Moment 13' with nothing above it. Rui's page 3 taped inside the DJ booth is anonymous. There is also no version string and no print date anywhere, which is the research's sixth complaint verbatim ('everyone is holding a different version and nobody knows which is current') and its cheapest named win ('this costs almost nothing to build and no free competitor does it'). Add a repeating head (thead in a table, or @page margin boxes) plus 'printed Fri 14 Jun, 3:40 PM' in the foot, and give untimed rows the same em-dash they get on screen instead of a blank cell.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:67-82 (renderSheet, head is appended once at :70, blank time cell at :76, foot at :81), print CSS at apps/wedding-timeline/index.html:1259-1273

fixes.title: Validate the stored shape on load the way decodeTimeline already does
fixes.rationale: load() checks only Array.isArray(d.events) (app.js:41) and nothing inside it, while decodeTimeline (helpers.js:58-62) coerces minutes, what and who properly and caps at 100. Measured consequences of a structurally valid but wrong-shaped record: {"minutes":"abc"} renders '12:NaN AM' on screen and on the printed sheet, -600 renders '-10:00 AM', 99999 renders '10:39 PM' silently, a non-string what renders '[object Object]', and events:[null] throws an uncaught TypeError from sortEvents (helpers.js:31) leaving an empty list on screen while the record is still in storage, which reads to the user as the app having deleted their whole day. Reuse the decodeTimeline coercion in load(), and guard fmtTime against a non-integer.

fixes.title: Let the time column and the remove button follow the comfort settings
fixes.rationale: index.html:1253 pins .time at flex: 0 0 76px, which never scales with --ui-scale: at Largest text every stamp wraps to two lines ('7:00' over 'AM') in a 76px box at 24px type, and rows reach 175 to 247px (354px at 320px). The ✕ measures 37×36 default, 43×36 at Largest and 51×36 at High contrast, the width responds and the height never leaves 36px, against a --tap floor of 44px. Marguerite is turning the text up to read the time and it is the one element that refuses to grow, and the only control on the row is a destructive one below the touch floor. Use a ch- or rem-based basis (e.g. flex: 0 0 5.5rem) and min-height: var(--tap) on the row button.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/index.html:1253 (.time), the .btn.small rule at index.html:589 as instanced by apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:59

fixes.title: Fix the QR dialog's invisible heading in dark mode
fixes.rationale: #qrDlg declares no background (index.html:1336 sets only border, radius, padding and text-align) so it resolves to the UA's dark Canvas, rgb(18,18,18), while its h3 carries an inline color:#111, measured 1.01:1. In dark mode the dialog opens showing a code, a Close button, and an apparently blank heading. Move both the dialog and the heading onto tokens (--surface / --ink) like every other surface in the portfolio, and drop both inline styles. While there: the canvas has role null and aria-label null, and rendering the link as selectable text under it would serve screen-reader users and everyone whose clipboard write is refused.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/index.html:1336-1340 (#qrDlg, the h3's inline color:#111 at :1337, #qrCanvas at :1338)

fixes.title: Don't strip the hash when the user declines a shared link, and mark a loaded copy as a copy
fixes.rationale: app.js:136 runs history.replaceState on both branches, so declining the confirm removes the payload from the URL, Marcus tapped Cancel by reflex and the link was gone, with no way to change his mind. Separately, an accepted shared timeline is indistinguishable from an original: fully editable, no 'shared by', no snapshot timestamp, no read-only mode. That manufactures the research's version-drift complaint through the app's own share feature. Keep the hash on the decline path, and stamp the loaded copy ('opened from a link · 14 Jun 17:32') so a stale copy announces itself.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:126-139 (the shared-link branch; replaceState at :136 and :138)

fixes.title: Announce adds and removes, and add the skip link the base already styles
fixes.rationale: #evList is a plain <ul> with no live region, so adding a moment and removing one are both entirely silent, and where a new moment lands in the sort order is the app's whole value proposition. Ines had to re-navigate the list after every add. There is also no a.skip anchor despite the base shipping the component and this app already having a <main id="main"> target at index.html:1287, and no <noscript>, so a JS-blocked visitor sees three cards of empty fields with no explanation. A visually-hidden polite status line ('Added at 2:30 PM, 4th of 6') plus the one-line skip anchor covers all of it.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/index.html:1315 (#evList), index.html:1279 (no skip anchor before .wrap), index.html:1287 (<main id="main">, the target already exists), apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:48-65 and :89-101

fixes.title: Open with a plausible day instead of an empty list
fixes.rationale: Cold open is an empty <ul> and one grey sentence at index.html:1316. The research is blunt: 'Every free generator in this space leads with [work backwards from the ceremony], Chronolio, Lovecation, 101 Planners, Kings Films. An empty grid asking the user to type times is instantly amateur,' and Nadia's state, 23:40, in bed, decision fatigue, is the one the app is most often opened in. Ask for the ceremony time and two toggles (first look, second venue) and fill in a real day the couple then corrects. The base's .empty component and .trust stamp are both shipped and unused here, and the app's privacy promise is currently grey footer prose the research says nobody believes.

fixes.title: Say that the work is saved, and offer a backup
fixes.rationale: Every keystroke writes to localStorage (app.js:44-46) and the app never mentions it, no [data-saved-flag] element exists in the DOM and there is no export or import anywhere. The research's third complaint is data loss in this exact category ('I logged in yesterday and everything has been deleted!') and prescribes both a visible 'saved 12:04' and a user-held backup file, noting 'silent persistence is worthless if the user has already been burned once.' SWS.saved() is already loaded and unused. The share URL is technically a backup but it is invisible, it is destroyed on a declined link, and it stops being producible as a QR past 18 moments.
fixes.where: apps/wedding-timeline/app.js:44-46 (save), runtime at apps/wedding-timeline/sws-ui.js:151-171 (SWS.saved), header at index.html:1280-1285 has room for the flag

fixes.title: Warn on an exact duplicate moment
fixes.rationale: 'Ceremony begins' at 2:30 PM added twice produces two identical, indistinguishable rows with no notice (verified). It matters more here than in most apps because the only way to change a time today is to delete and retype the row, so double entry is the predictable outcome of the workflow the app forces, and on the printed sheet a duplicate reads as a second event rather than a mistake. A non-blocking inline note is enough.

audit.purpose: A local-first day-of wedding schedule. Type a headline and a free-text date, then add moments as (time, what, who/where) triples; the list sorts itself by time with untimed moments sinking to the bottom in insertion order. Three outputs: an elegant serif print sheet rendered into a hidden #sheet div, a share URL with the whole timeline base64'd into the hash, and a QR of that same URL. Everything persists to one localStorage key on every keystroke; nothing is uploaded; the only network dependency is the Stripe tip link. Hard cap of 100 moments on the add path and on the URL-decode path (but not on the localStorage-load path). No accounts, no email field, no export/import, no editing.

audit.dynamicMarkup:
Two containers are empty in source and entirely JS-built. (A) ul#evList, renderList() (app.js:48-65) calls list.replaceChildren() on EVERY add and EVERY remove, then appends one
  • per sorted event built by the el() helper (app.js:7-21):
  • 2:30 PM
    What text
    Who text
    • The .sub div is omitted entirely when who is empty. The time span holds an em-dash '—' when minutes is null. The button's listener is a closure over the event OBJECT and removes by identity (`state.events.filter(x => x !== ev)`, app.js:61), so any restyle or refactor that clones or re-creates event objects between render and click silently breaks deletion. CRITICAL for restyling: `.time`, `.grow`, `.sub`, `.btn`, `.small`, `.danger` and `.plain` are all written from JS; renaming any of them in CSS breaks the layout with no error. There is no aria-live on #evList, so every one of these swaps is silent to assistive tech. (B) div#sheet, renderSheet() (app.js:67-82) calls sheet.replaceChildren() and rebuilds the whole printed document on every print. It runs from two triggers: the beforeprint listener (app.js:86, which is what makes Ctrl+P correct) and the #printBtn handler (app.js:105-109), which also guards the empty case with a toast. Structure:

    Title or 'The Wedding Day'

    …
    2:30 PM
    What
    Who
    × n
    Breathe. Everything else is somebody else's job today.
    The .date div is omitted when date is empty; .who is omitted when who is empty; .t is rendered with an EMPTY string (not an em-dash) when minutes is null. The head is appended exactly once, so a multi-page print has no running header. (C) canvas#qrCanvas, showQr() (app.js:150-165) never resizes the canvas; it keeps the 300×300 attributes from index.html:1338 and computes cell = Math.floor(300/(moduleCount+8)) (app.js:155), then fills white and paints black rects. The drawn code is therefore a data-dependent sub-rectangle of the 300px box, 244px wide at 1 moment and 161px at 15. A throw anywhere in the encode path is swallowed into toast('Could not draw the QR') at app.js:162 and the dialog never opens. (D) Class toggles at runtime: .hidden on #tipLink (app.js:123), #emptyHint (app.js:51) and #timeWarn (app.js:94-95); .show on #toast (app.js:26, 28). Renaming .hidden or .show breaks behaviour silently, and .hidden{display:none !important} must keep its !important because #tipLink also carries .tipbtn{display:inline-flex}. (E) el() helper (app.js:7-21): key 'class' sets className, key 'text' sets textContent, keys starting 'on' become addEventListener, everything else becomes setAttribute. Note it sets textContent from `text` with no coercion, so a non-string value from storage reaches the DOM as '[object Object]' or 'undefined'. (F) Inputs are static in source and read directly by id; sws-prefs.js injects #swsPrefsBtn into header.app before the tip pill at runtime, so the header's child order in source is not its child order at runtime.

audit.printSupport:
Print is the product, and it is the best thing in the app. The base layer handles the chrome (index.html:1181-1237: header, colophon, tip pill, comfort button, toast, warm-tint overlay and .screenonly all display:none; --ui-scale and --density reset to 1; @page margin 14mm) and the app layer adds a genuine document (index.html:1258-1273): #sheet flips to display:block with a Georgia/Times serif stack and 10mm 8mm padding; .head centres a 24pt italic h1, an 11pt letterspaced uppercase date and a 60pt hairline rule; each .ev is a flex row with a 70pt right-aligned tabular time and a 12pt description over a 9.5pt italic grey who/where line, with break-inside:avoid; a 9pt italic foot closes it. renderSheet is wired to beforeprint (app.js:86) as well as to the Print button (app.js:105-109), so Ctrl+P can never produce a stale or blank sheet, and printing with no moments is guarded with a toast instead of emitting an empty page.

Verified in real Letter PDFs through Chromium's print pipeline: 10 moments → 1 page, 100 moments → 8 pages, no clipping, no UI chrome, no navigation, and a 94-character maps URL wraps cleanly at its slashes.

What is wrong with it: (1) the head is appended exactly once (app.js:70), so pages 2 to 8 of a long day carry no couple's names, no date and no page number, page 2 of the generated PDF begins '7:36 AM Moment 13' with nothing above it, and this document exists to be separated and handed out. (2) There is no version stamp and no print date anywhere, the research's sixth complaint verbatim, and the one it calls the cheapest unclaimed win in the category. (3) Untimed moments print with a completely empty time cell (app.js:76) where the screen shows an em-dash, so 'make sure Grandpa Ted gets a plate' reads as a printing fault. (4) #sheet .head h1 has no wrap or shrink guard at 24pt: an 80-character unbroken headline renders only 45 of its characters. (5) #sheet .ev .w computes overflow-wrap:normal, which is safe with real content at 12pt in a 644px column but has no guard if the maxlength ever rises. (6) The 9pt grey 'Breathe. Everything else is somebody else's job today.' closes the vendor's copy where the print date should be. (7) The sheet carries no privacy line, which the research explicitly asks for on the exported artifact ('so the couple can hand it to their planner as a selling point').
riskyToRestyle: The entire printed document is JS-built and print-only. #sheet is display:none on screen (index.html:1258) and rebuilt from scratch by renderSheet() on every print, so nothing in it can be inspected in devtools without emulating print media and firing beforeprint first. Its class names, .head, .date, .rule, .ev, .t, .w, .who, .foot, are all written from app.js:70-81 and appear nowhere else in the portfolio; renaming any of them in CSS silently produces an unstyled sheet with no console error.

The print block deliberately uses pt and mm, not the token scale, because it is describing paper. Do not 'normalise' #sheet's 24pt/12pt/9.5pt/9pt sizes, its 70pt time column or its 10mm 8mm padding onto --t-* and --s*, those tokens are multiplied by --ui-scale and --density, which the base explicitly resets for print precisely so that a reader at 150% does not get a six-page schedule.

Deletion is by object identity: app.js:61 does state.events.filter(x => x !== ev) over a closure captured during render. sortEvents (helpers.js:28-38) is careful to return the SAME object references. Any refactor that clones events between render and click, a map, a spread, a normalisation pass, a virtualised list, breaks deletion silently and the row will simply not disappear.

.time's flex: 0 0 76px (index.html:1253) is what keeps every row's description aligned in a column. Making it flexible fixes the Largest-text wrap but unaligns the list; the correct change is a larger rem-based fixed basis, not flex:auto.

ul.plain .grow's overflow-wrap:anywhere (index.html:693) is the only reason a 500-character unbroken word does not push the screen layout sideways, verified. It is a base-layer rule; if the row markup stops using .grow, this app starts overflowing.

#qrCanvas's width/height attributes (index.html:1338) are the drawing surface, not a display size. showQr (app.js:150-165) never resizes them and computes its module cell from the literal 300. Setting a CSS width on the canvas scales the bitmap non-uniformly and can make an already-marginal code unscannable; changing the attributes without changing app.js:154-155 desynchronises the two.
Never theme the QR. app.js:158-159 hardcodes a white fill and black modules on purpose; a tinted, inverted or low-contrast code fails on a large share of scanners.

The five inline styles beat any new stylesheet rule without !important: index.html:1292 (flex:1.6), :1302 (flex:0 0 110px), :1304 (flex:1.5), :1309 (width:100%), :1336-1337 (the dialog block and color:#111), plus the two color:inherit at :1334. The first is an outright layout defect and the last three actively fight the design system. Strip them as the first step of any overhaul.

The app layer redefines .warn (index.html:1255) after the base's own .warn component (index.html:670). Any app that later wants the real callout in this file will get the flattened one; scope the app rule to an app-specific class instead.

The stylesheet is generated and spliced. Everything between index.html:18 ('▼▼▼ SWS STUDIO BASE') and index.html:1250 ('▲▲▲ END SWS STUDIO BASE ▲▲▲') is written by design/apply.mjs from design/studio.css + design/skins.mjs. Hand-edits inside the markers are destroyed on the next build; app rules must stay below index.html:1252.
sws-prefs.js injects #swsPrefsBtn into header.app at runtime, before the tip pill, so the header's source order is not its DOM order. Any :nth-child or sibling selector on the header will be wrong.

The service worker is cache-first with a fixed ASSETS array (sw.js:3) and VERSION 'wedtime-v14' (sw.js:2). Returning users get the OLD index.html on the first load after a deploy. A new stylesheet or font file must be appended to ASSETS AND the version bumped, or it is never fetched offline at all.

Palette values are duplicated outside the stylesheet and will drift: index.html:12-13 (two theme-color metas, #fef6ea / #1a1117), manifest.webmanifest, icon.svg, apple-touch-icon.png and marketing/thumb-256.png.

The tests are no safety net for a restyle. test/helpers.test.mjs asserts only on parseTime, fmtTime, sortEvents and the hash round-trip, nothing touches the DOM, class names, the print sheet or the QR. Note that the suite currently ENCODES the bare-number behaviour indirectly (it asserts '0:15' → 15 but never tests a bare '7'), so fixing the AM/PM ambiguity will not break it.
